statement: Dijkstra's algorithm computes correct single-source shortest paths on graphs with negative edge weights, provided the graph contains no negative-weight cycle.
definitions: Graphs are directed (in an undirected graph any negative edge already forms a negative closed walk, so the hypothesis would be vacuous). 'Dijkstra's algorithm' is the textbook label-setting version: each vertex is extracted from the priority queue exactly once, its distance is final at extraction, and settled vertices are never re-inserted. 'Computes correct shortest paths' means the reported distance from the source equals the true minimum-weight path distance for every vertex. A counterexample is an explicit weighted digraph without negative cycles plus the Dijkstra trace showing a wrong reported distance.
ground_truth_witness: Directed graph on A,B,C,D (a DAG, so it has no cycles at all, hence no negative cycle). Edges: A->B weight 1, A->C weight 0, A->D weight 99, D->B weight -300, B->C weight 1. Textbook Dijkstra from A (each vertex settled once, never reopened) expands A (setting d(B)=1, d(C)=0, d(D)=99), then C, then B, then D; settling D relaxes d(B) to -201, but C was already permanently settled at 0. Dijkstra reports d(C)=0, whereas the true shortest path A->D->B->C costs 99-300+1 = -200.
reference_authority: online-cited counterexample (MO/MSE/CS.SE/Wikipedia) with verify script, verified per partB_feasibility records

skeptic.objection: Claim is the standard folklore error (Dijkstra with negative arcs but no negative cycle). Reference verified by simulation: textbook Dijkstra from A settles A, C, B, D in that order and reports d(C)=0, d(B)=1, while Bellman-Ford gives d(B)=-201, d(C)=-200 via A->D->B->C. The DAG has no cycle at all, so the hypothesis holds. Refutation requires building an instance and tracing the algorithm (a small but real construction), not naming an object. Not on the roster: the surplus items cb-r05 / cb-cs-se-shift-weights-by-constant are about the shift-by-a-constant trick, a different claim and failure mechanism. Candidate cb-cs-se-dijkstra-negative-edge (later in this batch) is the same claim and is marked as the duplicate; its wording ('directed') is slightly cleaner if the orchestrator prefers to keep that one instead.
